newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-BELGIAN UNION OPPOSES BOSMAN BENEFIT MATCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BELGIAN UNION OPPOSES BOSMAN BENEFIT MATCH.

text.p: The benefit match long promised to Belgian Jean-Marc Bosman hit another snag on Tuesday when the Belgian soccer union said it would oppose the game.

The International Soccer Players' Union (AIFP) had said on Monday that the match, which had been repeatedly blocked by other soccer authorities in the past year, was very likely to go ahead in Brussels.

AIFP secretary-general Didier Roustan said after the union's first meeting with European Social Affairs Commissioner Padraig Flynn that it had contacted Brussels authorities about staging the game, but he was unable to give a date or further details.

Belgian soccer union spokesman Guido De Windt said: "One: we are not aware of it, two: there has been no request. Three: the soccer union's executive committee would have to decide but I fear it will be 'no'.
"In the current circumstances there is no way we would cooperate."
He noted Bosman was still sueing the union, and his former club FC Liege, for damages in connection with a blocked transfer to French team Dunkirk in 1990.
De Windt added that technically a match could be organised in the national King Baudouin stadium as it was owned by the city of Brussels and not the soccer union.
The Bosman case ended up before the European Court of Justice in Luxembourg after a local Liege appeals court asked it to interpret EU rules on free movement of workers.
The EU court ruled in favour of Bosman in December 1995 but the Liege court is still to decide on the amount of damages.
Last month the Spanish F.A. vetoed the benefit match being staged in Spain. Earlier plans to have it organised in Paris were also opposed and abandoned.
Bosman's case in the European Court of Justice brought about the end of quotas on foreign players in Europe, but also left the player financially stranded after a five-year legal fight.
